ca_tuolumne_meadows.blurb: Tuolumne Meadows is the high-country side of Yosemite National Park, a landscape of rounded granite domes rising out of pine forest. Roughly a dozen major domes and many smaller ones hold the climbing, with Lembert, Fairview, Medlicott and Stately Pleasure among the best known. Trad dominates, with a solid bouldering scene, some sport and a handful of alpine objectives. Most routes fall between 5.9 and 5.12, with a fair number of easier lines and a thin tail of harder ones. The rock is strong, knobby granite and granodiorite. Routes tend to be short to medium length, on faces or thin cracks, and the face lines can be runout with widely spaced bolts. Thanks to the elevation, the season runs mainly from June through September.

ca_apple_valley_area.blurb: Apple Valley Area gathers the crags around the town of Apple Valley in California's High Desert. Fairview Mountain is by far the largest part, with several formations reached on side trails off the main hill path, and it has a Joshua Tree feel with vertical, interesting rock. Horsemen's Center, Margheritaville and Fairview Valley East add more. Sport routes make up about half of the climbing, boulder problems are common, and there is a smaller amount of trad and top-rope. Grades center on 5.9 to 5.11, with a decent number of moderates and a modest top end around 5.12. Boulder problems mostly sit in the easy to middle range of V grades. Expect a desert hillside setting with plenty of variety.

ca_riverside_area.blurb: Riverside Area covers the climbing in and around the city of Riverside, in California's Inland Empire. Bouldering is the main event, centered on Mount Rubidoux, a boulder-strewn hill above the city, and on Box Springs Mountain Reserve, where granite walls hold short sport routes and cracks alongside many boulders. Riverside Quarry adds mostly sport climbing. Boulder problems skew easy to moderate, while the roped climbs are mostly 5.10 to 5.12. Rubidoux is known for thin, footwork-heavy problems on small edges, with a few top-ropes. The city often runs ten or more degrees warmer than the high desert, making it a handy cool-weather choice, though these are not destination crags.

wa_central_region.blurb: Central Region is the dry, sunny climbing of central Washington, led by Frenchman Coulee, better known as Vantage, and Banks Lake. Vantage has tall basalt columns with steep, pumpy face climbing, mostly sport with a fair amount of trad running up the cracks between columns. Its walls sit close to the road and it can fill up on warm weekends. Banks Lake feels more remote and is granite, with sport, trad, some boulders and a short winter ice season. Overall sport leads, trad follows, and bouldering and ice are minor. Grades center on 5.8 to 5.11 with a good number of harder lines. Both areas are valued for early and late season climbing, but midwinter can be bitterly cold.

ca_big_bear_lake_area.blurb: Big Bear Lake Area sits in the San Bernardino Mountains of Southern California and is the busiest part of that range for climbing, split into Big Bear North and Big Bear South. The range is mostly granite, ranging from excellent to a little grainy, similar to Joshua Tree, and routes are typically a single pitch. Bouldering and sport lead, with a good amount of trad plus some top-rope and a few alpine lines. Climbing is broad across the grades: plenty of easy to moderate boulder problems and roped routes from 5.6 to 5.10, with a solid core at 5.10 and steady numbers up to 5.12. Fisherman's Buttress on the south side of the lake is short and technical, with crimpy moves and mostly harder routes.

id_west_idaho.blurb: West Idaho spreads from the Boise area to the McCall and Riggins country, so the rock changes with the location. Black Cliffs, a few minutes from Boise, is columnar basalt with hundreds of sport and trad routes and the climbing is possible through most of the year. Swan Falls, on basalt beside the Snake River, is a bouldering area. Near McCall, granite crags like Pins and Needles offer trad and sport in the warm months, and Riggins Limestone provides sport on pale limestone. Bouldering is the largest share overall, with sport and trad close behind. Most roped routes fall between 5.8 and 5.11, with a decent number harder, and boulders cover everything from easy to V10.
